mainTopic: רבי עקיבא's double tithe on an אתרוג, and whether an אתרוג tithed by picking has its new year in תשרי or ט״ו בשבט
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about רבי עקיבא, who picked an אתרוג on the first of שבט and separated two different tithes from it. The ברייתא first says he did this to cover both בית שמאי (new year for trees on א׳ בשבט) and בית הלל (ט״ו בשבט). רבי יוסי בר יהודה gives a different reason: the argument between רבן גמליאל, who tithes an אתרוג by its picking like a vegetable, and רבי אליעזר, who treats it like a tree in everything. The גמרא asks how רבי עקיבא could take the stringencies of both בית שמאי and בית הלל. It answers that he followed בית הלל but was unsure of their date. It then asks why רבי יוסי בר יהודה's version mentions the first of שבט at all. רבי חנינא answers that the fruit formed before the previous ט״ו בשבט, and רבינא answers by reading the date as the fifteenth. Finally, רבה בר רב הונא says that according to רבן גמליאל an אתרוג's new year is תשרי, and the גמרא challenges him with a ברייתא that treats ט״ו בשבט as the dividing line.

steps.title: One tithe for each side: בית שמאי and בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that רבי עקיבא separated one tithe according to בית שמאי and one according to בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the tithes was according to בית שמאי, and the other was according to בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא about רבי עקיבא finishes by explaining why he separated two tithes: he wanted to cover both opinions about when the new year for trees begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית שמאי, ראש השנה for trees is א׳ בשבט, so a fruit picked that day may already belong to the new year. For בית הלל, it is ט״ו בשבט, so the fruit still belongs to the old year. Since the two years can need different tithes (like מעשר שני or מעשר עני), רבי עקיבא separated both.

keyTerms.meaning: The students of שמאי; here they hold the new year for trees is א׳ בשבט
The students of הלל; here they hold the new year for trees is ט״ו בשבט
Tithe: a portion of produce that must be separated

phrases.english: One according to the words of Beis Shammai,
phrases.notes: "One" means one of the two tithes רבי עקיבא separated from the אתרוג.

phrases.english: and one according to the words of Beis Hillel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, וְאֶחָד כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא about רבי עקיבא's double tithing that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא's two tithes were meant to cover both בית שמאי's and בית הלל's dates for the new year for trees.

steps.title: A different reason: רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says רבי עקיבא was really covering the argument between רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר, not the one between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: He did not act this way to follow the practice of בית שמאי and בית הלל. Instead, he acted this way to follow the practice of רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא gives a different explanation for the same story: the two tithes were because of a different argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The facts of the story stay the same: one אתרוג, picked on א׳ בשבט, two tithes. Only the reason changes. רבי יוסי בר יהודה points to a separate question: is an אתרוג tithed like a tree fruit or like a vegetable? The next step shows where that argument comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Practice or way of acting
He acted with it (with the אתרוג)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי בר יהודה is not saying the story happened differently. He agrees רבי עקיבא separated two tithes. He only disagrees about which argument made him do it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מִנְהַג בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל נָהַג בָּהּ,
phrases.english: He did not act with it according to the practice of Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel,
rather, according to the practice of Rabban Gamliel
and Rabbi Eliezer he acted with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִנְהַג בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל נָהַג בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reason given in step 1 and replaces it with a different argument that explains the same action.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא's two tithes covered the argument between רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: The משנה: an אתרוג is like a tree in three ways and like a vegetable in one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה where רבן גמליאל says an אתרוג follows tree rules for ערלה, רבעי and שביעית, but vegetable rules for tithes.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: An אתרוג is like a tree in three ways and like a vegetable in one way. It is like a tree in three ways: for ערלה, for רבעי, and for שביעית. It is like a vegetable in one way: its tithe follows the time it is picked. These are the words of רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the argument רבי יוסי בר יהודה mentioned, starting with רבן גמליאל's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a tree fruit, the tithe year is set by when the fruit began to grow. For a vegetable, it is set by when it was picked. רבן גמליאל says the אתרוג follows the vegetable rule for tithes, so an אתרוג picked on א׳ בשבט is tithed by the picking date.

keyTerms.meaning: Citron fruit
Fruit of a tree's first three years, which is forbidden
Fourth-year fruit, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed
The שמיטה year
Picking (harvesting)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the אתרוג's tithe year really is in doubt, which gives רבי עקיבא a second reason to separate two tithes.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: אֶתְרוֹג שָׁוֶה לָאִילָן בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּרָכִים,
phrases.english: As we learned: An etrog is like a tree in three ways,
and like a vegetable in one way.
It is like a tree in three ways:
for orlah, for fourth-year fruit, and for the Sabbatical Year;
and like a vegetable in one way —
that its tithing goes by the time of its picking,
these are the words of Rabban Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source text for the argument רבי יוסי בר יהודה mentioned.
steps.raayaObject: That there really is an argument between רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר about an אתרוג's tithes.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: an אתרוג is like a tree in everything
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר disagrees and says the אתרוג follows tree rules for everything, including tithes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: An אתרוג is like a tree in every matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with the other side of the argument: רבי אליעזר treats the אתרוג fully as a tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, the אתרוג's tithe year goes by when the fruit began to grow, like any tree fruit, and not by when it was picked. Since רבי עקיבא was not sure whether to follow רבן גמליאל or רבי אליעזר, the two opinions could point to different years, so he separated two tithes.

keyTerms.meaning: Tree
In every matter

steps.whatToRemember: There are two explanations of רבי עקיבא's two tithes: (1) a doubt between בית שמאי and בית הלל about the date of the new year for trees, or (2) according to רבי יוסי בר יהודה, a doubt between רבן גמליאל (tithe the אתרוג by picking, like a vegetable) and רבי אליעזר (tithe it like a tree).

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
An etrog is like a tree in every matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֶתְרוֹג שָׁוֶה לָאִילָן לְכׇל דָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted משנה with the opposing opinion, so the dispute רבי יוסי בר יהודה mentioned is fully shown.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר disagrees with רבן גמליאל about the אתרוג's tithe year.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The same משנה, quoting רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Can one follow the stringencies of two opposing opinions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא's double tithe using a ברייתא that says one may not combine the stringencies of בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really act according to two opposing stringencies? A ברייתא teaches that the הלכה always follows בית הלל. Someone who wants to follow בית שמאי may do so, and someone who wants to follow בית הלל may do so. If he takes the leniencies of both, he is wicked. If he takes the stringencies of both, the פסוק calls him a fool walking in darkness. He must pick one side and keep both its leniencies and its stringencies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks step 1. רבי עקיבא separated one tithe according to בית שמאי and another according to בית הלל, and that looks like taking both sides' stringencies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a person must choose one school and follow it completely, both where it is lenient and where it is strict. Grabbing only the strict rulings from both sides is called foolish. So רבי עקיבא's double tithe looks like the exact behavior this ברייתא rejects.

keyTerms.meaning: Stringency / stringencies
Leniency / leniencies
A wicked person
A fool

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not forbid being strict. It forbids picking and choosing from two opposing systems, taking only the strict side of each.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is a classic source for the rule that one may not combine the stringencies or leniencies of two disputing opinions.

phrases.english: But do we really act according to two stringencies?
phrases.notes: He means the strict side of two opinions that disagree with each other.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
The halacha is always like the words of בית הלל,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָרוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי — עוֹשֶׂה.
phrases.english: and one who wants to act like the words of בית שמאי may do so.
One who wants to act like the words of בית הלל may do so.

phrases.aramaic: מִקּוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּמִקּוּלֵּי בֵּית הִלֵּל — רָשָׁע.
phrases.english: One who takes the leniencies of בית שמאי and the leniencies of בית הלל is wicked.

phrases.aramaic: מֵחוּמְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּמֵחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל —
phrases.english: One who takes the stringencies of בית שמאי and the stringencies of בית הלל:
about him the verse says: "And the fool walks in darkness."

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: אִי כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי — בְּקוּלֵּיהוֹן וּבְחוּמְרֵיהוֹן.
phrases.english: Rather, either like בית שמאי, in their leniencies and in their stringencies,
or like בית הלל, in their leniencies and in their stringencies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to step 1 and challenges רבי עקיבא's conduct as reported there.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא separating one tithe like בית שמאי and one like בית הלל (step 1)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids combining the stringencies of both schools, and his double tithe seems to do exactly that.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא was unsure of בית הלל's date
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא really wanted to follow בית הלל, but he was unsure whether they set the new year for trees on the first or the fifteenth of שבט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא was in doubt about what he had learned. He did not know whether בית הלל said the first of שבט or the fifteenth of שבט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי עקיבא was not combining two opinions; he was handling a doubt about a single opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He planned to follow בית הלל only. He was not sure whether בית הלל's date was the first or the fifteenth of שבט, so he separated both tithes to cover both possibilities. Being strict because of a real doubt is different from mixing two systems.

keyTerms.meaning: His learned tradition, what he received from his teachers
He was in doubt
The month of שבט, when the new year for trees falls

steps.whatToRemember: Being strict out of uncertainty about one opinion is allowed. The ברייתא only rejects taking the strict side of two opposing opinions.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva was in doubt about his learned tradition,
and he did not know

phrases.aramaic: אִי בֵּית הִלֵּל בְּאֶחָד בִּשְׁבָט אֲמוּר,
phrases.english: whether בית הלל said the first of Shevat,
or whether they said the fifteenth of Shevat.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: a doubt within one opinion, not a mix of two opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא was taking the stringencies of both בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: He followed only בית הלל but was unsure of their date, so he was strict because of the doubt.

steps.title: Picking on the first of שבט only matters for בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי בר יהודה's version again and asks: if the fruit was picked on the first of שבט, that date only causes a problem according to בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: he did not follow the practice of בית שמאי and בית הלל. He followed the practice of רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר. But it happened on the first of שבט, so he was acting like בית שמאי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי בר יהודה's statement from step 2 again, this time to raise a problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story says רבי עקיבא picked the אתרוג on the first of שבט. The first of שבט is a new year only according to בית שמאי; for בית הלל the year does not change until the fifteenth. So the story still seems tied to בית שמאי, even though רבי יוסי בר יהודה said it had nothing to do with בית שמאי and בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Practice, custom
He acted with it (with the אתרוג)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion. The גמרא repeats רבי יוסי בר יהודה's words from step 2 so that it can challenge them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מִנְהַג בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל נָהַג בָּהּ,
phrases.english: He did not act with it according to the practice of בית שמאי and בית הלל,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִנְהַג רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר נָהַג בָּהּ.
phrases.english: rather, he acted with it according to the practice of רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר.

phrases.aramaic: בְּאֶחָד בִּשְׁבָט — כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי נָהַג בָּהּ!
phrases.english: On the first of Shevat? Then he acted like בית שמאי!
phrases.notes: The original story said he picked the אתרוג on the first of שבט, and that date is a new year only for בית שמאי.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאֶחָד בִּשְׁבָט — כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי נָהַג בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי יוסי בר יהודה's version (step 2) and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי בר יהודה's claim that the case did not involve the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Picking on the first of שבט creates a change of year only according to בית שמאי, so the case still seems to depend on their view.

steps.title: The fruit formed before the previous ט״ו בשבט
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא explains that the אתרוג's fruit formed before the fifteenth of the previous שבט, so the year had changed even according to בית הלל. The first of שבט is mentioned only because that is when the event happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא, and some say רבי חנניא, said: We are dealing with an אתרוג whose fruit formed before the fifteenth of the previous שבט. By rights the same would be true even if it had been picked earlier, but the actual event happened this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining when the fruit formed. Once that is known, the case works even according to בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fruit formed before the fifteenth of the previous year's שבט and was picked on the first of the following שבט. So a new year for trees (that earlier fifteenth) passed between formation and picking by everyone's count. רבי אליעזר goes by when the fruit formed, and רבן גמליאל goes by when it was picked, so they assign it different tithe years. Any picking date after that earlier fifteenth would raise the same question, and the first of שבט is mentioned only because that is when it actually happened.

keyTerms.meaning: Formed, budded (the first stage of the fruit)
Of the other one, meaning the previous one
We are dealing with
And by rights it would be so
The event that happened, happened this way

steps.whatToRemember: The fruit formed in one year and was picked in the next, even according to בית הלל. So רבי עקיבא's two tithes were about רבן גמליאל (picking) and רבי אליעזר (formation), not about בית שמאי and בית הלל.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said, and some say it was Rabbi Chananya:
Here, with an etrog
whose fruit formed

phrases.aramaic: קוֹדֶם חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר דְּאִידַּךְ שְׁבָט עָסְקִינַן.
phrases.english: before the fifteenth of the other Shevat, we are dealing.
phrases.notes: "The other שבט" means the שבט of the year before. The fruit formed before that date and was picked on the first of this year's שבט.

phrases.english: And by rights it would be so even before then,
phrases.notes: He means that even if it had been picked earlier than the first of שבט, the same doubt would come up.

phrases.english: but the event that happened, happened this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּאֶתְרוֹג שֶׁחָנְטוּ פֵּירוֹתָיו קוֹדֶם חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר דְּאִידַּךְ שְׁבָט עָסְקִינַן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case: specifies when the fruit formed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The year change at the first of שבט only works according to בית שמאי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fruit formed before the previous ט״ו בשבט, so the year changed even according to בית הלל. The first of שבט is mentioned only because that is when the event happened.

steps.title: רבינא rereads the story: ט״ו בשבט, and a doubt between רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers the question from step 7 differently. He reads the ברייתא as saying the fruit was picked on the fifteenth of שבט. רבי עקיבא gave both tithes because רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר disagree, not because of בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Put the two corrections together and learn it this way. It was not the first of שבט, it was the fifteenth of שבט. And he was not following both בית שמאי and בית הלל; he was following both רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a second answer to the question about why the first of שבט matters. He fixes the wording of the ברייתא so the problem goes away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא kept the date as the first of שבט and explained it as just when the story happened. רבינא changes the date to the fifteenth, which is בית הלל's new year. Now רבי עקיבא's doubt is a different one: whether to follow רבן גמליאל (the אתרוג goes by when it was picked, like a vegetable) or רבי אליעזר (the אתרוג follows tree rules for everything). So he gave both tithes.

keyTerms.meaning: Combine and teach; read the text with these changes put together
Practice; here it means the rule of a certain opinion

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not saying רבי עקיבא mixed the strict rules of בית שמאי and בית הלל. In his reading, both sides of the doubt agree with בית הלל that the new year for trees is the fifteenth of שבט.

phrases.english: Ravina said: Combine and teach:
phrases.notes: Literally 'wrap and learn.' He means to read the ברייתא with both changes that follow put together.

phrases.english: It was not the first of Shevat
rather, it was the fifteenth of Shevat,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מִנְהַג בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: and it was not the practice of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel
that he followed with it,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִנְהַג רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
phrases.english: rather, the practice of Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer
is what he followed with it.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא: according to רבן גמליאל, the אתרוג's new year is תשרי
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא draws a conclusion from רבן גמליאל's view. If an אתרוג is tithed like a vegetable, by the time it was picked, then its new year for tithes should be תשרי, like vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: Since רבן גמליאל said an אתרוג goes by when it was picked, and is tithed like a vegetable, its new year is תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement opens a new discussion. רבה בר רב הונא takes רבן גמליאל's rule one step further and fixes the אתרוג's new year as תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל said only that the אתרוג follows the picking date, like a vegetable. רבה בר רב הונא reasons that if it is like a vegetable in that way, it should also share the vegetable's new year, which is the first of תשרי, not the fifteenth of שבט.

steps.title: A ברייתא treats ט״ו בשבט as the dividing line for an אתרוג
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה בר רב הונא with a ברייתא. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר goes by the picking time, yet he still treats the fifteenth of שבט, not תשרי, as the line between the old year and the new year for an אתרוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises an objection. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: If someone picked an אתרוג on the eve of the fifteenth of שבט before sunset, and then picked more after sunset, he may not separate תרומה and tithes from one batch for the other. This is because תרומה and tithes are not separated from the new crop for the old, or from the old for the new. If the third year was turning into the fourth year, he gives מעשר ראשון and מעשר עני from the third-year fruit, and מעשר ראשון and מעשר שני from the fourth-year fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack רבה בר רב הונא's claim that the אתרוג's new year is תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא goes by when the fruit was picked, just like רבן גמליאל. Even so, picking a moment before or after the start of the fifteenth of שבט changes the tithe year. That shows the new year for an אתרוג is the fifteenth of שבט, not תשרי, which goes against רבה בר רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: Separating תרומה and tithes

steps.confusionAlert: Sunset on the 'eve of the fifteenth' is the start of the fifteenth itself, because a Jewish day begins at night. So the two batches really fall on two sides of the new year.
